bottleneck: Brain organoids now show coordinated electrical activity resembling preterm infant EEG, raising the question of whether they can suffer — with no way to answer it. If organoids are conscious, growing them as disposable research tools is morally fraught; if they are not, restricting the research wastes medical progress and costs lives. The uncertainty is total because consciousness has no validated measurable marker even in adult humans, let alone in disembodied tissue. Ethics boards debate guidelines while organoid complexity grows monthly, and each advance in realism deepens the dilemma without providing the instrument to resolve it.
current_state: Ethics boards debate guidelines while organoid complexity grows. No framework resolves the moral-status question, and research continues under precautionary ambiguity.

sources.title: The brain might not create consciousness after all

title: Brain organoid sentience unmeasurable
why_it_blocks: Organoids could model disease and test drugs without animal suffering — or they could be suffering minds in dishes. The inability to tell paralyzes both ethics and research, the worst of both worlds.
